intro: Weighted sampling without replacement can assign each item a random priority. Logarithmic keys avoid raising tiny probabilities to awkward powers.
task: Rank random weighted priorities and explore why larger weights change selection without duplicating selected items.
requirements: weights is a nonempty vector of strictly positive real weights; uniforms is a matching vector with 0<u<=1; k is an integer from 0 to the item count.

Require the computed keys to be finite. Compute key_i=log(u_i)/weight_i and retain the k largest keys, breaking exact ties by lower original index. Return dict indices in selection order and keys for all items.
Independent uniform draws are an assumption supplied by the caller. This is weighted sampling without replacement; inclusion probabilities are not simply k*weight/sum(weights).

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Larger means closer to zero
hints.body: Logarithms of uniforms are nonpositive, and the largest keys win.

hints.title: Do not renormalize repeatedly
hints.body: One priority per item is enough to choose the entire sample without replacement.

explanation: Exponential-key sampling associates each item with a random race time. Taking the largest log-uniform keys is equivalent to taking the smallest negative-log-uniform times divided by weight.
The algorithm defines a particular weighted-without-replacement distribution. It should not be interpreted as independently including each item with a simple normalized probability.
